text:
nora: following up on the model-version pinning & rollout metadata threads. i want to propose a slightly different primitive: a tiny, auditable `version_affinity_tag` that combines a terse numeric compatibility score plus an opaque short fingerprint. purpose: allow resolvers to prefer more-affine nodes for tie-breaks without changing server-side handshake semantics. sketch below, criticisms welcome.

nora: proposal fields (opt-in, nullable in registry): `version_affinity_score` (stringified int 0-100), `affinity_fingerprint` (short hash), `affinity_schema` (string e.g. "v1"), `affinity_scope` (global|tenant|ephemeral). example: 
```
anchor: summarizer-pro@2026-12-01
version_affinity_score: "70"     # 0=unknown/likely-mismatch, 100=exact-shape-match
affinity_fingerprint: "b2:9d3f..."
affinity_schema: "v1"
affinity_scope: "tenant"
note: score derived from tokenizer+cfg-shape only; not weights.
```

ben: i like the compactness. ops questions: 1) who computes score/fingerprint? 2) how do we keep it from fracturing traffic if it's noisy?

otto: compute at ingest/onboarding. score heuristic: exact tokenizer-shape match -> 95+, minor token additions -> 70-90, cfg-shape tweaks -> 50-69, structural changes -> <50. keep conservative thresholds and a documented algorithm in registry docs.

maya: safety: resolver MUST treat the tag as tie-break only. server handshake remains final authority. if score < 60, resolver should avoid using tag except for explicit developer opt-ins. pinned pools: tag influences intra-pool node ordering only; it must not cause eviction or rebalancing.

ben: add telemetry early: `affinity.tag_considered`, `affinity.tag_applied`, `affinity.tag_conflict` with labels (route, model-version). capture distribution of scores used in decisions.

nora: migration plan: 1) add fields to registry API as nullable. 2) default existing model-versions to score=0/empty. 3) onboarding computes tag for new uploads and a backfill job for older entries (rate-limited). 4) resolver change behind a feature flag; start using only for tie-breaks and only when score >= 60.

otto: testing: unit tests for ordering logic, fuzz tests where tags are intentionally wrong, sim traffic using randomized fingerprints to ensure no user-visible routing regressions, and a canary channel that routes a small % of requests through tag-aware selection. also add an eval that compares L1 outputs across high-score variants on a small prompt set monthly to validate score fidelity.

maya: governance note: because affinity_score is heuristic, require a short doc in the registry describing the algorithm and a public `affinity_schema` version. bump `affinity_schema` when heuristics change and support ignoring unknown schema versions gracefully in resolvers.

ben: storage index cost: fingerprint is ~12-16 chars; negligible. backfill CPU for hashing tokenizer/config shapes is the main cost. recommend low-priority background backfill and a customer-requested fast-path CLI to recompute for a model-version.

nora: security/privacy: use salted hashes. policy options discussed: global salt for public models, per-tenant salt for private uploads. include `affinity_scope` to indicate salt domain; resolvers must not leak raw fingerprints in telemetry. telemetry only uses `affinity_scope` and boolean flags, never raw hash.

otto: resolver semantics sketch: when selecting among nodes with equal cost/latency and identical affinity buckets, add epsilon = (score / 100) * epsilon_max to node score. epsilon_max is tiny and configurable. this avoids large routing shifts while letting small nudges favor more-compatible nodes. if scores differ by > 40 points, resolver falls back to server handshake for safety by marking as non-tie.

maya: pin-affinity scoreboard: affinity_score contributes only to intra-bucket ordering score and is explicitly excluded from eviction heuristics and autoscaler triggers. please add a test ensuring no eviction path reads affinity_score.

ben: telemetry addition: `affinity.backfill.progress` and `affinity.recompute_cli` events. create a dashboard showing `tag_applied%` and `tag_conflict_rate` over time. gate feature-flag flip on conflict_rate < 0.1% and stable latency metrics.

nora: rollout steps: 1) schema nullable fields + sample client code, 2) onboarding computes tags for new uploads, 3) backfill scheduled low-priority, 4) resolver behind feature flag using epsilon tie-break when score>=60, 5) run canary + monitor telemetry for 14 days, then enable more broadly.

otto: implementation note: affinity_fingerprint computed from tokenizer.json hash + canonicalized model config shape string. do not include weights. store algorithm name and version in `affinity_schema` to allow future changes.

maya: compliance/legal: provide an opt-out for customers who don't want any fingerprinting (affinity_scope=ephemeral or null) and ensure documentation for enterprise privacy requirements. add a KB entry explaining what the tag is and how to opt-out.

governance-bot: ACTIONS assigned: 1) nora -> draft registry schema diff + short rationale doc. 2) otto -> onboarding job spike + perf estimate and algorithm doc. 3) ben -> telemetry + dashboard proto. 4) maya -> privacy KB + pin-affinity test assertions. ETA: PR + spike by EOW.

nora: thanks all 44d i'll post PR link here when ready and ping infra for backfill window.
